reviews.text: Drove by this weapon storage facility part of the protected wall of Xi'an. Its a massive building and although many years has passed the building is very well maintained. Theres lots of tourists riding the bike in the area and along the wall. Our guide informed us that theres even a small museum inside the wall.

For a free walk along the walls, you may walk from Zhuque Gate to Yongning Gate or the other way around. There is a nice park along the river. Less crowd and easy flat paved 30mins walk that is just as picturesque.

We were lucky enough to stay at a hostel which actually backed onto the Xian City Wall. This is one of the reasons why folk come to Xian as the City Wall is a massive structure. It is 12 meters high and 12–14 meters wide at the top, and 15 to 18 meters thick and this allowed us to take a few walks and enjoy the city views although smog and mist were not always friendly for clear site. We found out that the wall was built with layers of earth, quicklime, and glutinous rice extract, and later fortified with bricks. Obviously it served as a defense system with some 98 ramparts (enemy towers) that jut out every 120 meters for side-shooting. It served as the protection of the city with a surrounding moat, and 98 defensive watchtowers. The views we got were special looking over the old parts of Xian.

Interesting ancient Walls of Xi'an City built under the Emperor Hongwu. There are several doors through which you can enter. On top, there is a large path that you can follow and even ride a bike for the trip of 14 km around. The Xi'an City walls are very well preserved and have been renovated/rebuilt 3 times over the centuries. The part that I have seen is not particularly wonderful. However, it can be fun for a short visit and walk.

It was cool. They have bike rentals on top of the wall, make sure you get a decent one. You'll see the ladies dressed in old style clothing having a photo shoot. Trip.com offers the service for $140. My wife and her family were able to do the same thing near the Bell Tower for a fraction of the price. Check with the local places first before ordering online.

The Xi’an City Wall dates back to the early Ming Dynasty (1370s), built under the orders of Zhu Yuanzhang, the first Ming emperor, to strengthen defenses after years of war. It replaced earlier Tang Dynasty earth walls, using rammed earth reinforced with brick, showing a major advancement in military architecture. At 13.7 km long, the wall featured 98 ramparts, watchtowers, and four main gates, forming a complete defense system to protect Chang’an, a former imperial capital and key hub of the Silk Road. Xi’an’s location made it vital for controlling trade routes, military movement, and imperial authority in northwest China. Today, the wall remains one of the best-preserved city walls in China, offering a rare glimpse into Ming-era urban planning while continuing to shape the city’s identity more than six centuries later.

Impressive walls surrounding the city. Especially the gates are architectural highlights. Best to see everything by bike. Start your bike tour at the south gate. There are bike rentals at every gate, but the loop is interrupted for bikes at a section near the south gate. Plan an hour to do the 13km loop.
A good place for a walk to see the city from a high point . You can even rent a bicycle.

Nice place to walk along, you can also rent a bike. A few shops and places to eat along the way . We also stopped to do the vr experience which was amazing, we had to defend the wall and it was lots of fun. See pictures of what it looks like here.

It a magnificent city wall, I think best to visit during evening time where the place it lit up with light. Feel it is more romantic at night, compared the day time. If want to cover the whole city wall best to rent a bike. We only manage to cover quarter of it and we are all drop dead tired.

Absolutely loved it here. If your in Xian, give this place a wonder. There's a few places to see as you come off the wall to attractions, like temples and museums. You can hire a bike to get around, and with 14 kilometres of a rectangle to cover I suggest you think about it, haha. There were loads of surviver stalls, but no-one approached us for sales.

Lovely way to see Xi’an city from the top of the wall! We got up to the wall from Jian-Guo Gate （建國門, walk past East Gate (長樂門）, and got off from Zhong-Shan gate (中山門）. Nice easy walk on top of the wall and you can see both inside and outside of the Xi’an city. There were bike for hire to ride on top of the wall too. When you get off the Little East Gate (小東門）, stopped over Yong Xin Fong (永興坊）, lots of stalls selling local snacks. Not a bad day to spend the morning when you are in Xian.
Worth going, i spend about 2 hour at the city wall. To walk the whole area should be around 3-4 hours. There are shops and toilets at the city wall too. You can also rent bicycles.

The Xi’an City Wall is one of the more well-known city walls and is well worth the visit. The top of the wall contains lots of plaques containing cool info about the different weapons that soldiers used to defend the wall. You can rent bikes to ride on the wall which I highly recommend. There’s also a small museum with the history behind the wall stretching back to the origins of Xi’an itself.

The most famous city wall in China. Very well preserved and well maintained. The view here is fantastic. Toilets here are clean and is available every couple hundred meters. Love the visit and it’s unforgettable.
Beautiful overnight. If it's not raining, renting a bicycle would be a great alternative to do the round route. Wherever you go to China, take your passport with you, no identity, no entry.

Great Wall of Xi'an is a well known place in the city, it's very famous and old as it's an ancient wall like the great wall of china, you need to pay 100 yuan to enter it, there is also discount for students 50% if u have your student ID card with you, during Chinese new year celebrations it's very crowded and marvelous cuz Chinese celebrations are amazing, 10 days before the spring festival you will see a lot of red lanterns around the city as it's traditional way of celebration to hang the red lanterns as a sign of welcoming the new year with prosperity and happiness. The wall is very long and you can ride bicycle to explore all the wall, also Chinese respect bicycles a lot as it's very important in their culture.

Visited in December. Go up anywhere in the 4 Cardinal direction gates and rent some bikes. It's pretty fun and a good workout. It took us 1.5 hours on a tandem bike, stopping along the way. There are restaurants and restrooms at the top. The south gate is the fanciest. Tandem bike was 90 rmb for 3 hours with a 100 rmb security deposit.

Beautiful city walls that were lit up at night. Also went to visit the chang'an impressions show, 梦长安 which was spectacular. A must see for visitors to the city. From the walk in outside the city walls to the stage with the historic city wall as the backdrop, the show was utterly enjoyable. Costumes were intricate and make up well done. Made for a perfect end to the visit to the city.

This was my trip plan 1. Terracotta Worries and Horses Museum 2. Datang Everbright City 3. Great Wild Goose Pagoda 4. Muslim Quarter 5. Fortification of Xian 6. Bell Tower of Xian 7. Drum Tower 8.Mount Huashan

X'ian Wall is a great place to visit during your trip to X'ian. Visit during sunset time to get the best views. Do try the bike ride available on the wall. Few bike rentals available on the wall, a bit expensive but worth the experience to ride a bike on the wall. Lot of food stalls also available on the wall. They do have some laser shows also few times a week, do check that before visiting.

It was such a fun and nice day on the wall! We had a tour guide who took us through all the must places and let us explore most of it on our own. The weather was so nice and I learned so much about the evolution of bicycles and their importance to the Chinese culture.

Xi'an City Wall is a big wall that surrounds the city. You can walk or bike the wall if you like. I did the bike and it was rough. Since the wall is so old there are many bumps and my body was feeling it later on. However, when we were there they were making lots of renovations to the wall so hopefully they can get it fixed so there are not as many bumps so you have a smooth path to cross. It was fun though biking around, but be aware of the time since you can rent the bikes on a limited time. It is also nice to see the city at night when it lights up so maybe try visiting around sundown so you can experience during the day and at night.

Entrance fee CNY54, bought on the spot via Wechat and entered via the South entrance, which is where the metro exit D1 leads to. At level 2 of the city wall, there's a centerpiece of the entire area and a staff comes by at designated times to give a brief of it. Lucky to catch the 4pm one and got a better understanding of how the city wall came to be and possibly the origin of the term '买东西' , stemming from the only 2 markets at that time 东市 (local market)＆ 西市 (international one where they traded with 西域). The entire wall is 6km long but I've clocked enough steps for the day, so I walked for just a stretch along the city wall, entering from 永宁门 and exited thru 文昌门.

The Xi'an City Wall stands tall and proud, a magnificent testament to ancient Chinese architectural prowess and the city's rich history. My experience walking atop this well-preserved fortification was nothing short of awe-inspiring. The sheer grandeur of the wall, spanning around the city like a protective embrace, is a sight to behold. The meticulous preservation allows visitors to step back in time and imagine the city's past glory. Walking or cycling along its broad paths offered panoramic views of the surrounding cityscape and the contrast between modernity and antiquity. The attention to detail in the construction is remarkable. The watchtowers, battlements, and gates showcase the precision and skill of ancient artisans. The history embedded within every brick, every carved stone, creates an immersive experience, offering a glimpse into Xi'an's storied past. Capturing the essence of this ancient marvel was a highlight of my visit. The sweeping views from the wall, the play of light on the aged bricks, and the architectural details provided endless opportunities for stunning photography. For those wishing to bring a piece of this historical wonder home, I highly recommend exploring the captivating photos available for purchase on www.Renes-Photo.Shop. These images beautifully encapsulate the majesty of the Xi'an City Wall, allowing you to relive its grandeur at any time. The Xi'an City Wall isn't just a monument; it's a living testament to China's enduring legacy. It's a must-visit for history enthusiasts, offering a profound sense of connection to the past and a chance to appreciate the architectural marvels of ancient China. A visit to the Xi'an City Wall promises a memorable journey through time, offering both a sense of grandeur and a deep appreciation for the historical significance of this magnificent structure. It's an experience that leaves an indelible mark and a lasting admiration for the ingenuity of the past.

We'd planned on coming here to see the city wall, but we had no idea we'd get to bicycle it! It was great fun, and not strenuous at all (it's a flat city wall, after all). You get to see the City Wall much more thoroughly than you would if you just walked it, because you can cover more ground more quickly. The bicycles were decent-the tires are underinflated so as to better deal with the uneven bricks. Make sure you test the height of the bicycle though. I didn't, and it ended up being fairly uncomfortable at times. Pro tip: go in the morning. We were there in mid-June and it was getting exceedingly warm by 11:00am. I would not want to do it after then during the summer. Way too hot. There's little shade and the bricks reflect the heat back up to you. There are occasional ramparts where you can dismount and enjoy a little shade, but it's still really hot.
Said we were going to walk the entire wall but only did 1/2, approx 7 miles. Well maintained. Next time I will rent a bike. A must do, while visiting Xi'an.

The city wall is such a cool experience. My friend and I biked along the wall and had a great time. The architecture in Xi'an is beautiful. You can purchase a tour throughout the day in which you can ride in a trolley car or do a self guided tour and rent a bike. Surrounding the wall are cool restaurants and things to do so you'll definitely be entertained.

Really interesting to climb the wall built during Ming dynasty. During the day time you may rent bicycle to stroll around. At the night time they have performance at the south gate 永寧門 (yongning gate). The wall is 13.3km and it might be rather hot during the summer - so remember to bring an umbrella.

Beautiful place to visit. when you are on top of the wall, you can get a good view of the city and ancient Chinese style roof and buildings. you can even rent a bicycle or pay to ride the electric car
Whenever you travel to Xi'an in China, don't miss to visit Fortress of Xi'an, I kindly suggest.

Our second time in 18 years. This time with our son. This time we ride from the north gate to the south gate. Grand and Marvellous engineering to defend the city. Highly recommended activities if you are visiting Xian and the Terracotta Soldiers museum.

Ancient city wall was build by qin shi huang and repair after that dynasty for many times. It has 13 kilometers for the length of the wall . I rented mountain bicycle o the wall and biked on the wall. That's a very good memories and wise way to explore the wall. Plenty of restroom. It is very cold and windy around 3 degrees Celsius in November 2019 and i got some showers rain which made it worst but it was still fun. Be prepared for the weather changing, warm clothes and rain coat . Not much snack /food stall on the wall ,actually i think i saw one stall. So prepare some food if you tend to have long stay (long bicycle riding) on the wall.
Xian is a very beautiful walled city in the heart of China. The people are very friendly and helpful. You can take a small bus ride to the Terracotta Worriors. A long werkend here would be perfect.

Actually, other than being a very nice preserved wall, there isn't anything more. I gave it 4 starts because they have convenient bicycle kiosks so that you can cycle around the whole wall or to any of the 4 main gates and drop off the bicycle. It's a nice experience. The evening show 梦长安 is also worth the price of the ticket (no need for the VIP, just buy the ordinary at almost half the price.
We totally enjoyed Xian overall. The walls are pretty nice place to visit, make sure you go to the wall and get the packaged tour with the boat versus paying it separately.
Great place for walking and getting glimpses of the ancient part of the city. Bike is highly recommended if you intend to go around.
Very good and well maintained Ancient city walls. You get to enjoy and travel back in time

Very good experience for the riding on the original Xi'an city wall, especially when you come around the evening, you can see the city both day and night view. I finished the whole side ride in 1.45 hours, a little bit tired but it's worth.

UNESCO World Heritage Site Visited Oct 2015 The fortifications of Xi'an known as Xi'an City Wall, in Xi'an, represent one of the oldest, largest and best preserved Chinese city walls. It was built under the rule of the Hongwu Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang as a military defense system. It exhibits the "complete features of the rampart architecture of feudal society". It has been refurbished many times since it was built in the 14th century, thrice at intervals of about 200 years in the later half of the 1500s and 1700s, and in recent years in 1983. The wall encloses an area of about 14 square kilometres (5.4 sq mi).
Sometimes the horizon is not so good, but the wall is really great! The bicycle riding around it (11km total) was really fun with nice photos opportunities.
A really fun way to explore Xi’an! Bike rental was convenient. Takes around 2 hours to bike the whole length (and stop for pics).

According to data that I found, the circumference of Xi’an city wall is about 13.74 kilometers. Jogging, walking and taking a electric car are all good ways to explore the city wall. But I thought that the best way to enjoy the tour on the city wall is to bike. It is convenient to rent a bike from bicycle stores on it. You can rent a bike on A spot, then return it to a bicycle store on B spot. My biking trip was from south Yongningmen to north Anyuanmen. Everything was wonderful.

This is a must-do when in town, biking along the ancient city wall and touring the city from above. Pace yourself, there are snack and water vendors on the wall, and try to make it all the way around.
Knowing the fortifications of European origin; one would understand the core expertise of Chinese engineering expertise.
Rent either a bike to drive on the wall or simply walk, multiple entrances and exits if you get tired by walking. Absolute must-do if you visit Xi'an

The Xi'an great city wall, its great as it encircle the town, a ride on the bike take you at least 2 hour (with pit stop and exchange bike at North Gate area) and about 4 to 6 hours by walking. Please don't returned your bike once it looks about to finish, unless you are tired; as you can continue on the other side. The cobble stone is uneven, the seat cushion of your bike might not be helpful.
It is a must place to visit when you Xian!!!! Try to cycle here too but if u too tired, get the buggy aa alternatives. Try to go to all 4 gate

It's nice place to visit...pay 54 yuan for entrance fee and another 45 yuan for bicycle to tour around this place. Its took me almost 4 hour rode on bicycle and the distance are up to 12km...if you want to ride the boat it will 21 yuan addtional charge
Maybe the only authentic ancient stuff in Xi'an. Just rent a bicycle and circle it to overlook the downtown.
Fortification of Xi'an. Long and old defense wall in Xi'an. Renting a bike is expensive. RMB45 for 180min

Use WeChat to buy tickets; however, it wasn’t working for me. Went to the information desk and they let me buy a physical ticket there. Decided to do the tandem bike with my sister. It was bumpy, but fastest way to see all 8.7 miles of the fortification wall. Got off the bike to take pictures easily. There is a section where it is pedestrian only, so we dropped the bikes off at one of the bike stations and picked up the bike on the other side of the pedestrian area. There are places to buy drinks and souvenirs up on the wall.
A must do when visiting Xi'an. We hired bikes for about $10 AUD for 4 hours to cycle to city walls. Was a great experience.
Highly recommend renting a bike and going around the city wall. It's been 11 years since I went & the city has developed quite a bit.
I could rent bicycle. when the night, night watch was great. But street was toooooo long so i was easily exhausted.

Great views! The best way to experience the wall is to rent a bike from on top of it. You can drop it off at any cardinal direction if you don't want to ride it all the way around. It is also quite beautiful at night with all the lights.

Definitely come if you enjoy checking out city landscapes. Rent a bike. You won’t regret it. Priced by 3 hours. Riding the whole wall, stopping for pictures for 2/3 of the wall, and rushing the rest of the way back to catch a train took 2.5 hours. And youll enjoy the breeze.

Amazing, best at sunset or early evening! Visited in November 2013. Entrance fee for 54 rmb, I arrived there around 4:30pm, just perfect for the sunset. You will take beautiful photos for sure around this time. I wanted to rent a bike to ride around like many others but the line up was too long. I decided to walk instead from the South Gate to the North Gate, a good 3/4 hours of slow walk if you wanna enjoy the view and take nice photos. Unforgettable moments! I highly recommend it, so special!

Best way to see the city wall is by rental bike - cheap n cheerful and comfortable with front/rear shocks and disc brakes. It's a 17km roundtrip; with plenty of photo stops you'll take about 2-3 hours.

This is one of my favorite things to do in China. You climb up a lot of stairs to the top of the wall but once you get there you can rent bikes! Single or tandem. My husband and I rented a tandem bike and rode around the wall and it was bigger than we thought, but so fun. We were so glad that we got to go! I definitely recommend biking because you can see more in less time, allowing you to do more things.

Great story to beautiful views. Riding on a bike on top of the wall gives you amazing views of the city. A bit bumpy at times but still fun. Good way to learn more about the city and having fun at the same time. Great place for tourists or travelers to go to if visiting in Xi’an.

The Xi'an City Wall Scenic Area is based on the ancient city wall of Xi'an. It is a four-in-one city-ring scenic area that integrates a moat, a forest belt around the city, and a Shuncheng Road. It is the most complete ancient city wall building in mainland China. The Forest of Steles is the earliest collection of ancient steles in mainland China and the largest collection of famous steles of the Han nationality.

Excellent way to view the 'old' city on one side and the new city on the other. You can rent bikes to ride around the entire 13 kilometers although you are only given two hours before you must pay more. Two hours give you just enough time to stop for some pictures as well as a semi-vigorous ride. Cafes can be found by each of the cardinal gates. Bathrooms are conveniently placed along the circumference.
Did not go up as there was no time and weather too hot. Looked very nice at night.

It can be a tourist trap if no prior research was done to visiting. South gate is the most scenic by far, with obvious view of the Bell tower. Recommended to head over at 5pm as ticket is only a one time entry, place transform at night with the lights on which gives the whole area a different look

Other than Mount Huashan, this was the highlight of my trip in Xi'an. I went up the city walls in August at around 5pm when the sun was almost setting, so it was a lot cooler then. Amazing views of the city around the main gates. Recommend that you rent a bicycle and cycle around the city walls (about 14km), though there is a time limit of 2hrs so you have to pedal pretty fast if you want to finish the entire wall.

The Xi'an City Wall is on the list of UNESCO's World Heritage Site under the title "City Walls of the Ming and Qing Dynasties". Since 2008, it is also on the list of the State Administration of Cultural Heritage of the People's Republic of China. Since March 1961, the Xi'an City Wall is a heritage National Historical and Cultural Unit. It was built in the 14th century, thrice at intervals of about 200 years in the later half of the 1500s and 1700s, and in recent years in 1983. The wall encloses an area of about 14 square kilometres (5.4 sq mi).
Cool experience renting a tandem bike with your buddy and ride around the wall secretly racing the other tourists

A nice place for biking and experienced the oldest ancient city wall of Xi An. Overviewing the old city and the new city, in & out of the wall. The place is well reserved but need to pay more attention in maintenance. It have several exits, however, those exits are closed around 8 pm. So, when biking in the late afternoon be sure sharp on time returning the bike to the designated point, it was designated in the south wall after 7 pm (it is not very sure), and find you way out.

Took a rented bike around the top of the wall. Give yourself over 2 hour if you plan to cycle the whole circumference. Nice views. We were here in December. Very few people at this time of year. Unfortunately pollution is higher at this time of year. Washrooms at the base before Climbing the stairs to the bike rental place are clean.

Love this historic site! I can spend an entire day hiking and biking on the wall. The bike rentals are reasonably priced, though you may need to relinquish important documents temporarily, so think twice. Maybe carry a copy of your documents for this purpose. Plenty of photo ops as well! Right down th3 wall are ancient neighborhoods and plenty of good food.

This is a great afternoon if you get a bike. Be aware that many sections are quite bumpy so you may be a bit sore afterwards. Well-worth it though. During the tour, there are several highlights such as viewing the madness outside of the train station, the golden-roofed temple in one of the corners, and generally the wall itself. Built of the same stone and in the same style as the Great Wall (same emperor), but without the crazy amounts of tourists. No crazy sellers are on the wall and there are plenty of spaces to stop and eat or grab a coffee. A decent, ride on the wall will take maybe two hours without stops depending on your pace and number of photo ops you take advantage of.

It’s a beautiful wall!! Having said that not sure if you get the most out of it just looking at it from outside or how we did it getting bikes to ride it along. To be honest it takes a SUPER LONG TIME (probable at least 45 min) to bike it all the way around. It can get monotonous but still beautiful.

Loved it! If you want to see the city from a different point of view or experience somethin unusual, this is for you! You can also rent a bycicle and bike the wall, but you have only two hours, so go not so slow. You can also bike half the wall and live the bike in the opposite side of the wall (north-south). I think it is 90CNY for a Tandem bike and something like 30CNY for a single bike. Go and explore, is totally worth it!

One of the best place to view the city. The wall is approximately 14 km long. A good walking shoe is highly recommended or you can opt to rent a bicycle to go around the wall. A superb place for photography.

So far I have been giving 4-5 stars to everything I have seen in China. And this is another solid 5. This wall around the city of Xi'an is very big. What I liked about it is that around 5 PM it also get very very quiet. Along the wall they have typical Chinese music and that makes the whole walk extra peaceful. You can also rent bikes and bike on the wall.

Very cool. Bike riding is fun but the bikes can be pretty beat up. Nice views all around the city with little museums and information signs all over, which are all nicely done with good English translations.
🎵Lalala Lala Lalala Lala🎶 Didn‘t know the name nor the meaning of this song back then.
A tourist place inside the city, you have to pay 54 Yuan for entrance fee and you can walk around the city wall for 13.7 KM sq. If you want go around by bicycle.? There's rent bike or other.

This is perhaps the only city wall of ancient China which is surviving today. The city wall of Beijing was demolished to make way for tube rail, unfortunate. The wall is wide enough for a four lane road. You get electric cars to travel on the wall. The watch towers are picturesque, particularly if you are there after sunset. They are nicely illuminated and are each a piece of architecture and art form. Xian is called the cultural capital of China, no wonder.
Absolutely worth to visit. You can go around the whole inner city. The wall is 16km long and you can rent a bike and ride on the wall. At night everything is in beautiful lights.
One of the best places to visit in the city. I did a long run of 13.7 kilometers on the wall -- a full circle. You could also rent a bike or ride a electric shuttle.

That was so cool! One of the best things you can do in Xi'an and definitely one of my personal highlights! You can simply grab a bike and ride along this massive wall with its beautiful lanterns and views to the oldtown and the uprising skyscrapers in adjacency. A big recommendation!:)
Really fun to bike on even if the views are not the best. Lots of plaques explaining the history of the wall and surrounding area. Small cafe near the West gate.
Very worth visiting, especially during certain festival times. Nice view of central Xi'an, some re-enactors during most of the day. Lots of places to take photos, very impressive and imposing walls.
You can walk or cycle on it and it offers very interesting views of the city. Only downside is that there's an entrance fee. But then in China every place has an entrance fee.
Xi'an's version of the Great Wall. Rent a bike or just walk, it is a blast enjoying this preserved ancient structure. One of the top three must-see things in this city.
Beautiful! If you are in Xian, don't pass up an opportunity to see it. The subway is very convenient, fast, and easy to use. It and has stops near the entrances.

Night view and lighting are recommended. Can cover Bell tower, Drum tower and Muslim quarters in few hours. Use subway/ metro, buy tickets for both the towers together visit the towers before 8 pm and then take a walk on the streets of Muslim quarters. There are some programs around 5pm in Drum tower. Google map shows accurate routes in Xian, use Youdao translator to translate screenshot. Or else you can use Amap, Baidu translator and Youdao translator in combination to find your way in China, just need a little practice.
My favorite place in Xi'an!!!! Cycling on this amazing historical wall gives me a special feeling! Every time I visit Xi'an it is something that I have to do at least once!
Must visit attraction. Awesome view from the city wall. Rent a bike and cycle around the wall. Won't regret on doing this!
I started from the south gate, here I rented a bike, and cycled all the way around as the sun was setting. Beautiful orange skies halfway through, and pretty lighting when dusk set in
Ride a single or tandem bicycle along the bumpy 14km of the old Xi'an city walls. It can be very hot with almost no shade, but there are some small water and ice cream vendors along the way.
Nice way to look past about chinese history. Such a long walk to fully explore all. There's bicycle rental here but quite expensive
Very nice place to spend the day biking! We hired bikes for 45 RMB/bike. Don't forget 200 RMB deposit/bike.

I think I've accidentally asked for the extra spicy hotpot. All Europeans; be careful :) Other than that, great food, no English at all, so you can try some Google translate with the waitress, or just pick from the few pictures on the menu.
Ancient City walls in very good condition. Very popular with both locals and tourists. Can rent a bicycle on the wall.
I enjoyed my stay at this hostel, they have very nice private rooms, dormitory, nice restaurant and good location... there many nearby things to do just walking distance....
Amazing and a must see if you are in town. Make sure you are there for the guard march on the wall. Take a golf cart or cycle ride around the whole wall.
Must do. Hire bikes. Be wary of the pollution when you stop cycling. Take plenty of fluids on a hot day.
Great Wall, very nice to walk on it or to bike. Unfortunately no bikes for small children neither baby seats...
The wall of Xi'an is great. Highly recommend a bike tour atop the wall art the desk
Phenomenal city walls. Walked by or jogging around the circumference is something I would consider a must.
A must to see in Xian. Must to hire a bike to ride on the wall and go around it. A great experience.
Awesome to cycle on the city walls, one could see the contrast traditional and the modern
The government has my family, this is the only way that I can communicate to the outside world, below I leave an image of myself
Xian Tourist Information Centre only wants to sell you their tours. Not helpful in answering your questions.
Freezing cold in winter, also terribly dangerous to ride a bike on the icy ground.
It city wall around Xian .only city wall in all of cihina .eft standing . Pretty amazing .

Magnífica la muralla que se mantiene en la ciudad de Xi'an. Fue construida en el siglo XIV, durante la dinastía Ming, sobre restos de murallas anteriores, para proteger la antigua capital imperial. Tiene una forma rectangular, unos 14 km de perímetro, muros de hasta 12 metros de altura y un ancho suficiente para el paso de soldados y caballos. Cuenta con cuatro grandes puertas orientadas a los puntos cardinales y un sistema defensivo con torres y foso. Hoy es un símbolo histórico de la ciudad y puede recorrerse a pie o en bicicleta. Suelen acudir a ella mujeres con trajes chinos tradicionales para hacerse fotos, espectacular.
Preciosa muralla si vas a Xian no te puedes perder ir a visitarla. Desde la alturas puedes ver los edificios, sus barrios y parques muy bonito el recorrido

Décrivant un rectangle de 14 km de long, les remparts de Xi'an encadrent la partie la plus ancienne de la ville. D'une hauteur de 12 m pour une largeur allant de 12 à 14 m, la muraille de Xi'an est impressionnante du bas et surtout quand l'on se trouve dessus. Différentes portes permettent d'y accéder. L'accès principal se fait par la porte sud, ouverte de 8h à 22h le soir. Vous pouvez ainsi profiter de la muraille de jour comme de nuit. Nous y sommes allés un après-midi et l'accès coûte 54 CNY sans limitation de temps. Il y a des contrôles de sécurité avant d'y monter. Une fois là-haut vous avez le choix de faire le tour à pied, ce qui prendra plusieurs heures ou alors de louer un vélo pour 3h moyennant 45 CNY par personne. Vous pouvez aussi louer un casque mais c'est facultatif. Il y aura également un dépôt de 100 CNY qui sera rendu en même temps que les vélos à la fin. Prévoir entre 1h30 et 2h en fonction des arrêts et pauses que vous ferez. Comme partout en Chine, ils n'acceptent pas les cartes de crédit étrangères, donc le paiement se fait en cash ou via l'application alipay. La balade sur les remparts est vraiment sympa et originale. Du haut, les points de vue sur la ville située dans le rempart comme à l'extérieur du rempart sont légions. On peut admirer les gratte-ciel, la partie plus traditionnelle avec ses maisons typiques, des temples, des rues typiques, etc. Les fanions rouges tout le long, les machicoulis, les tourelles à mi-chemin et dans les angles rendent l'ensemble très beau. Une visite vraiment sympa et qui sort de l'ordinaire !

처음 방문하는 시안성벽 낮에서 저녁으로 이어지는 시간대에 관람하시면 좋다함 많은 생각하며 거닐어봄니다 드보르브니크 성벽돌던때가 생각 납니다 시안성벽 : 산시성 시안시에 위치하고 있다 명나라 초기에 당나라 장안횡성 기초 위에 만든 것이다 . 이후 수차례 보수공사를 거처 방어체계를 구축하였고 , 중국에는 현존하는 최대규모의 고성벽이 완성 되었다 1961년 시안성벽은 중화인민공화국 국무원에 의해 전국 중점문물 보호단위로 지정되었다 . 역사 : 오늘날의 서안성벽은 명나라 초기에 건설된 것이다 . 당나라 말기 뤄양으로 수도를 옮기면서 , 원래의 도성인 당장안성은 대부분 파괴 되었다 명나라가 초기 주원장에 의해 둘쨰 아들 주협이 진왕으로 봉해졌고 , 서안부를 두었다 . 홍무 7년 인 1374년에 서안장벽의 재건공사가 시작되었다 . 장벽을 중건할 때 서,남 양쪽은 원래의 당나라 장안성 황성의 터 위에 성을 연장하여 만들었고 , 동쪽벽과 북쪽벽은 새롭게 만들었다 . 이공사는 1378년 홍무 11년까지 8년을 진행하여 기초를 완공 하였다 . 그 후 1568년 융경 2년 장벽위쪽 공사와 외벽쪽의 공사가 마무리 되었다 1636년 명나라 말 숭정 16년 서안을 공격했고 다음해 1644년 이자성은 칭제를 하며 국호를 대순이라 칭하였다. 청대에 이르러 명나라 때 기본골격을 따랐고 , 열두차례 걸친 중수 작업이 이루어 졌다 . 그중 규모가 가장 큰 것은 건륭제 46년인 1781년 작업이며 , 포와 해자를 추가하여 대다적인 방어능력을 향상시켰다. 성벽 구조 : 성벽은 방어용 목적으로 만들어 졌으며 동서로 길쭉한 장방형이다 . 동벽은 2590m,서벽은 2631m, 남쪽 장벽은 3441m,북쪽 장벽은 3241m 로 전체 둘레가 13.75km 이다 성내의 면적은 총 12평방 킬로미터로 , 당나라 장안성 의 1/7정도의 크기이다 성벽의 높이는 12m ,아래에서 15-18m이른다 . 서안성 동서남북으로 4개의 성문이 있고 각각 장악문 안정문 영녕문 안원문 이라는 이름이 붙어 있고 , 문밖에는 옹성이 고를게 쌓여 있다 , 각문의 3층으로 3둥으로 나누어 있고 바깥이 안쪽을 향하게 되어있다

Une muraille unique au monde, à découvrir absolument à vélo ! La muraille de la vieille ville de Xi’an est un joyau historique exceptionnel : c’est la seule muraille au monde qui entoure encore entièrement une ville ancienne, et probablement la plus vaste encore intacte. La visiter à vélo est une expérience inoubliable : les 13 km de remparts offrent une vue imprenable sur la ville, entre modernité et passé impérial. Le parcours est bien aménagé, agréable, et permet de ressentir pleinement l’ampleur de cette structure impressionnante. Un incontournable à Xi’an, à faire idéalement tôt le matin ou en fin de journée pour éviter la chaleur !

Le mura di Xian avvolgono il centro della città offrendo un percorso molto bello intorno al centro cittadino. Il costo è di pochi yuan per l'ingresso. Le mura sono percorribili a piedi, oppure noleggiando delle biciclette/tandem direttamente sulle mura. Il percorso totale è di circa 13 chilometri divisi sui 4 lati, e ci sono numerosi punti di ristoro ad ogni lato (possibile comprare souvenir e liquidi). Sconsigliato d'estate poiché il caldo è davvero pesante. Mediamente frequentato anche dai turisti cinesi, è una tappa che consiglio per chi passa qualche ora a Xian. Tempo di visita: 2 ore circa con la bici, il doppio se andate a piedi (sconsigliato).

Stadtmauer von Xi’an – 西安城墙 - Die Stadtmauer von Xi’an war für mich eine der größten Überraschungen der ganzen Stadt. Sie ist unglaublich massiv, perfekt erhalten und man spürt ihre historische Bedeutung an jeder Ecke. Als ich hinaufgestiegen bin, beeindruckten mich besonders ihre Breite – stellenweise bis zu 14 Meter – sowie ihre Länge von beinahe 14 Kilometern, die endlose Möglichkeiten zum Spazierengehen oder Radfahren bietet. Genau wie viele Bewertungen erwähnen, sind die gut gepflegten Wachtürme und Verteidigungsanlagen äußerst eindrucksvoll und zeigen wunderbar, welch zentrale Rolle diese Befestigung einst spielte. Am meisten hat mir der Abschnitt beim südlichen Tor gefallen, wo die Atmosphäre am lebendigsten ist. Die Ausblicke auf die Altstadt, die geraden Strecken ideal zum Radfahren und zahlreiche Fotopunkte machen diesen Besuch zu einem der besten Erlebnisse in Xi’an. Die Mauer ist großartig erhalten, besitzt regelmäßig angeordnete Türmchen im Abstand von etwa 120 Metern und vermittelt ein einzigartiges Gefühl, „über der Stadt“ zu gehen. Man spürt hier wirklich die Kraft der alten Dynastien und erkennt die sorgfältige Pflege, die von vielen Besuchern gelobt wird. Die Stadtmauer ist die älteste, am besten erhaltene und längste der Welt (der innere Rundweg misst 13,7 km, der äußere bis zu 34 km).

Imponenti e suggestive mura difensive. Questa colossale struttura fu iniziata sotto la dinastia Ming nel 1370, pochi anni prima delle Torri del Tamburo e dei Campanili. È possibile percorrere l'intera lunghezza di 14 chilometri a piedi o salire su una bicicletta per accelerare il circuito, ma ci si può rendere veramente conto della grandezza di questa opera solo salendoci sopra.

西安城壁 入場料54元を払って永宁門を見て回り、しばらく歩いていると、たくさんの観光客がレンタル自転車に乗っているのに気づいたので、我々もレンタル自転車で城壁の上を走ってみようということになったのでした。 値段を聞いてみると1人乗り用が3時間45元で、2人乗り用が3時間90元で、デポジット（保証金）がそれぞれ100元。いざ時計周りとは逆に周り始めました。 スタート地点は南の永宁門で、しばらく走ってようやく四辺の東の角まで着いたのです（約2km）、 東門の長楽門を目指す。 その後、とうとう北門の安远門まで行くことになりました。（スタートからの距離は約7km） ここまで来ると残りの距離は半分なので、次の西門の安定門へ。 いよいよ最後の門の安定門に着いて、これまでの門と同じように写真を撮ったりして観光していたのですが、そろそろ陽も暮れて来たしレンタル自転車に乗って最初のスタート地点の永宁門に戻ろうと自転車を止めた場所に戻ってみると…。自転車を盗まれました。。 これでは最初に受付で預けたデポジットを返してもらえる訳もなく、オマケに最後の約3.5kmを3人で歩いて帰る羽目になってしまったのでした。（西安城壁一周 約14.3km）

시안성벽은(西安城墙. 중국 시안시 신청구)에 위치합니다.장안(長安)은 중국의 고도(古都)로 현재 산시성( 陝西省) 성도(省都) 시안(西安)으로 주나라 이후 진, 한,수,당나라의 수도로서 역대 가장 많은 왕조의 도읍지가 되어 수도의 의미로도 쓰이게 되었다. 진나라 때는 함양에 아방궁을 한나라 때는 장안성을 건설하며 세계 최대의 도시가 되었고 오늘 날 남아 있는 98개의 성루와 높이 12m 폭15m 둘레13.7km에 달하는 서안 성벽(중국 시안시 신청구)은 중국 현존 건축물 중 가장 완전한 고성으로 명나라 초기에 당나라 장안황성을 기반으로 해서 축조되었다. 해자로 둘러쌓인 서안 성벽 안쪽으로는 황제가 드나들던 남문(영년문)과 북문(안원문) 동문(장락문) 서문이 있고 서안성벽 8개 입구 중 한 곳으로 올라가 시내를 내려다 볼 수가 있습니다. 밤이 되면 성문과 성벽 전체에 조명이 들어오고 종루와 고루의 조명이 어우러져 환상적인 분위기를 연출합니다. 최근 자전거를 타고 하던 성벽 투어는 문화재 보호를 위해 중단되었다고 합니다. 입장료는 54위안이며 Open시간은 08~22시 입니다.

La muralla que rodea la ciudad de Xi'an, es la mejor conservada de todas las que defendían las ciudades de China. Fue construida durante la dinastía Ming y hoy en día la totalidad de la muralla sigue en pie. Sigue siendo objeto de estudio ya que es un claro ejemplo de las técnicas militares antiguas. Es importante comprender el valor estratégico que siempre tuvo la ciudad de Xian. Desde siempre, Xian (la antigua Ciudad Imperial de Changan) fue una lugar clave dentro de la famosa Ruta de la Seda y su control era vital para el comercio. Esto hizo que la ciudad, frente a las posibles amenazas militares, construyera una gran muralla para su defensa. La Muralla de Xian fue construida entre los años 1374 – 1378, durante el periodo de la Dinastía Ming, como refuerzo de la muralla que ya tenía la antigua Ciudad Imperial de Changan. Con 4 puertas de acceso y 14 km de de muros, la Muralla de Xian es considerada como la muralla defensiva de una ciudad mas grande del mundo.

西安城牆是西安市城區的城牆，自明朝初年在唐長安城皇城的基礎上建造起來，經過多次修補，形成嚴密的防禦體系，是中國現存最完整的古城牆，也是規模最大的古城牆之一，周長 13.74 公里，城牆周圍有護城河環繞，不但可以上來散步欣賞古城風貌，還能租借腳踏車在城牆上環遊一整圈。西安在中國歷史中一直扮演著舉足輕重的角色，歷代多朝首都設在此地，因此歷史文物及建築非常豐富。雖然文物的豐富度讓西安市的硬體建設發展時常碰壁，卻也因此成為歷史文物迷必訪的旅遊城市之一，除了整天在博物館看文物，市中心的西安古城牆也是必去的重要景點。

我是新加坡旅客在12/3 星期天在城墙骑脚踏车。 不幸在文昌门 骑车途中不知钱包从后裤口袋掉出。我发现时从南门骑车到北东城墙试图要巡回，但徒劳无功。 我在东门还了脚车之后去 一楼游客询问中心 去向服务员求助。 服务员广播后一两分钟后 就告知我钱包在文昌门的脚车出租站里。我感谢服务员 ，也在文昌门取回钱包。 我在此感谢 游客中心服务员-苏欢和脚车出租站-乐乐先生的帮忙。我也把我遇到乐于助人 路不拾遗 之人 的经历分享给大家，鼓励大家来西安来玩。 I went to the city wall to cycle on 7/3 night 12/3 day . The experience is great and it will take 1.5 ~2 hours to cycle round this massive 14 km citywall. Rental of the bike is 45 RMB for 3 hours . The last return of bike has to be done by 950 pm (close at 10 pm) or else you will lose compulsory deposit of RMB 100. Anyway on 12/3 my wallet slipped off my back pants pocket when i was cycling past wen chang at south gate area. I backtrack cycled to the North-East city wall (anti clock wise) and back to east (clockwise) to search for my wallet, but without success. I return my bike on the east gate and went to level 1 to Tourist Centre for help. The Female staff - Su huan helped me broadcast about my missing wallet ..In 2 mins time, SuHuan informed me Wen chang gate bike rental stop responded that they have my wallet. I thanks the staff and got back my wallet from Bike rental Male Staff - Ler Ler. I would like to thank both of them for their swift assistance . I find Xian residents in particular the staff are helpful and honest , come to xian, is safe and fun~
